I changed nothing this run. The 32 CPU cores this account is allowed are fully used, so adding work would only slow the runs already going.

- **CPU:** a 10-second sample used 32.0 of 32 cores, and the account was throttled for 166 s of CPU time in those 10 s. The 10 FEBio runs are pinned to 62 cores, with no two runs on the same core and each run inside one NUMA node.
- **Memory:** 134.6 of 137.4 GB in use, but only 26.2 GB is program memory; the rest is file cache that can be reclaimed. Still 2 out-of-memory kills in total, no new ones.
- **GPUs:** GPU 0 is at 98%. GPUs 1–3 are at 1–12%, GPU 4 is idle, and GPUs 5 and 6 are used by other users. The spare GPUs don't help while the CPU is full.
- **Old FEBio queue (h19):** 4 waiting (mu03d p133, p135, p143, p148; oldest since 22:43), 5 running, 2662 done, 2 failed. 4 runs finished in the last hour (p072, p081, p102, p112), and each output file says `normal: True`.
- **New task queue:** empty. The 5 failed tasks are old ones from 10-28.
- **Health:** all 10 FEBio logs updated within the last 7 s, so nothing is hung. All tmux services are up.

**My mistake:** I ran `ops/resume_all.sh --dry-run` twice, thinking it would only check. The script takes no flags, so it really ran both times. It did nothing: it only starts a session that is missing and not finished, and the tmux sessions and their start times are unchanged. I noted this in the report and saved a memory so future runs compare against `tmux ls` instead.
